description: C++ overlay stability + Damage fact value. Two independent C++-only fixes bundled into one feature because they share the same CI build. (A) FIX 1 - the Damage fact currently shows only the label 'Dano' with an optional '(xN)' hit count and ignores dmg_multiplier, so the user sees no value. Make the Damage branch of formatFact() include the multiplier when present. (B) FIX 2 - overlay text flickers because pipeline.cpp calls overlay::setTranslations() every OCR cycle and a zero-match cycle overwrites the panel with an EMPTY list, blanking then repopulating. Make the displayed translations sticky: never clear on a zero-match cycle; only replace shown content when a new non-empty matched result arrives, with a hold timeout so stale tooltips clear after the user moves away. CANNOT be compiled in this Linux sandbox (Windows/MSVC/vcpkg only); verify by strict manual review of scope/types/braces/header declarations. A past build failed C2065 on a block-scoped variable used outside its block - do NOT repeat.
steps: FIX 1 (Damage value) in src/translation/skill_tooltips.cpp, formatFact(): SPLIT the current combined `type == "Damage" || type == "Heal"` branch so Damage and Heal are handled distinctly. For Damage: start with the translated label (fallback 'Dano'); when hasNumber(fact, "dmg_multiplier") append the multiplier using numToStr(fact["dmg_multiplier"]) and when hasNumber(fact, "hit_count") with hits>1 include the hit count. Use a clear PT-BR format, e.g. line = 'Dano: <mult>x (<hits> golpes)' when both present, 'Dano: <mult>x' when only multiplier, 'Dano (x<hits>)' when only hit_count>1, and bare 'Dano' otherwise. For Heal: keep the existing behavior (label fallback 'Cura' or keep current 'Dano' fallback consistent with label; Heal has hit_count but no dmg_multiplier) - append '(x<hits>)' when hits>1. Reuse the existing numToStr() and hasNumber() helpers (numToStr collapses integral floats and trims trailing zeros, so 0.39 stays '0.39' and 2.5 stays '2.5'). Do NOT fabricate an absolute damage number (the API does not provide it).

FIX 2 (flicker) in src/overlay/imgui_overlay.cpp: introduce a hold mechanism around g_translations. In the anonymous namespace add a timestamp tracking when g_translations last held a NON-EMPTY matched set (e.g. `std::atomic<unsigned long long> g_lastNonEmptyTick{0};` or a plain ULONGLONG guarded by g_translationMutex). Modify setTranslations(): under g_translationMutex, compute whether `entries` contains at least one matched entry with non-empty translated text; if it does, replace g_translations and update the last-non-empty timestamp (GetTickCount64()); if it does NOT (zero matches this cycle), do NOT overwrite g_translations - instead leave the previous content in place, UNLESS the hold timeout has elapsed (GetTickCount64() - lastNonEmpty >= holdMs) in which case clear g_translations so a stale tooltip eventually disappears when the user moves away. Keep all access under g_translationMutex for thread-safety. Ensure F8 hide (g_visible / toggleVisibility) is unaffected - hidden overlay still renders nothing. Do NOT reintroduce raw/unmatched OCR display; matched-only stays.

FIX 2 config wiring: add an overlay hold-time config key so the timeout is tunable. In src/config/config.h add member `int m_overlayHoldMs = 5000;` (5 seconds) plus a getter `int overlayHoldMs() const;` declaration (place near ocrIntervalMs). In src/config/config.cpp: implement the getter (shared_lock pattern like ocrIntervalMs()), add `json["overlay_hold_ms"] = m_overlayHoldMs;` in save(), and add `if (json.contains("overlay_hold_ms")) m_overlayHoldMs = json["overlay_hold_ms"].get<int>();` in loadInternal(). In config/bronco_config.json add `"overlay_hold_ms": 5000` (keep valid JSON, comma placement). In imgui_overlay.cpp setTranslations(), read the hold timeout from bronco::Config::instance().overlayHoldMs() (config.h is already included there).

Manual C++ review before finishing: for every edited function confirm (a) all braces balance, (b) any new variable is declared in the scope where it is used (no block-scoped var referenced outside its block - this caused a prior C2065), (c) numToStr/hasNumber calls match their existing signatures, (d) the new overlayHoldMs() getter is declared in config.h AND defined in config.cpp, (e) no new headers are needed beyond what each file already includes (imgui_overlay.cpp already includes <mutex>, <atomic>, config.h, and uses GetTickCount64 which is available via Windows.h already pulled in via imgui_overlay.h).
acceptance_criteria: In formatFact(), a Damage fact with {"hit_count":6,"dmg_multiplier":0.3} produces a PT-BR line that visibly includes the multiplier value (e.g. contains '0.3'), not a bare 'Dano'.
A Damage fact with only dmg_multiplier (hit_count==1) still shows the multiplier and omits the '(x1)' hit count.
Heal facts continue to render with '(xN)' when hit_count>1 and never reference dmg_multiplier.

setTranslations() no longer clears g_translations when called with a zero-match entry list; the previous matched content persists until either a new non-empty matched result arrives or the hold timeout (overlayHoldMs, default 5000ms) elapses.
overlay_hold_ms is present in config.h (member + getter), config.cpp (getter body + save + load), and config/bronco_config.json, consistent with the existing ocr_interval_ms wiring.
F8 toggle still fully hides the overlay; matched-only display is preserved (no raw OCR text rendered).
verification: Manual review confirming brace/scope/type/signature correctness (no compiler in sandbox).
Confirm every new/changed symbol used across the .cpp is declared in the corresponding .h (overlayHoldMs in config.h).
Confirm config/bronco_config.json remains valid JSON after adding overlay_hold_ms.
findings:
FIX 1 (Damage): split the combined Damage||Heal branch in formatFact() (src/translation/skill_tooltips.cpp). Damage now surfaces dmg_multiplier via numToStr as 'Dano: <mult>x', appends ' (<hits> golpes)' when hit_count>1, falls back to '(x<hits>)' when only multi-hit, and bare 'Dano' otherwise. Heal keeps hit_count-only behavior with fallback label 'Cura' (previously shared the 'Dano' fallback). numToStr/hasNumber signatures reused unchanged (both take const nlohmann::json&). No absolute damage number fabricated. Dataset already contains dmg_multiplier/hit_count so no regen needed.

FIX 2 (flicker): setTranslations() in src/overlay/imgui_overlay.cpp is now sticky. Added ULONGLONG g_lastNonEmptyTick (guarded by g_translationMutex) in the anonymous namespace. setTranslations computes hasMatched using the SAME filter render() uses (entry.matched && !translated.empty()); on a matched cycle it replaces g_translations and refreshes the tick; on a zero-match cycle it leaves prior content and only clears once GetTickCount64()-g_lastNonEmptyTick >= overlayHoldMs. All g_translations access stays under g_translationMutex. F8 (g_visible) and matched-only rendering untouched.

Config: added overlay_hold_ms (default 5000) wired exactly like ocr_interval_ms - m_overlayHoldMs member + overlayHoldMs() getter decl in config.h, getter body (shared_lock) + save() write + loadInternal() json.contains guard in config.cpp, and "overlay_hold_ms": 5000 in config/bronco_config.json (validated as valid JSON with python3 json.load).

Verification: C++ cannot be compiled in this Linux sandbox (Windows/MSVC/vcpkg only). Performed strict manual review: braces balance in both edited functions; no block-scoped variable used outside its block (the Damage-branch 'hits' is function-block scoped and used within; Heal has its own block-scoped 'hits'); numToStr/hasNumber calls match existing signatures; overlayHoldMs() declared in config.h AND defined in config.cpp; no new headers needed (imgui_overlay.cpp already has <mutex>/<atomic>/config.h and GetTickCount64/ULONGLONG via Windows.h from imgui_overlay.h). config/bronco_config.json confirmed valid JSON.
